relative = a person in your family
cousin = the child of your aunt or uncle
nephew = the son of your brother or sister
niece = the daughter of your brother or sister
get married = to become husband and wife
get divorced = to legally end a marriage
household chores = regular jobs at home such as cleaning
do the washing-up = to wash plates and pans after a meal
take out the rubbish = to carry the bin bags outside
hang out = to spend time with friends in a relaxed way
stay in = to not go out in the evening
go out = to leave home for social reasons
sleepover = a night spent at a friend's house
best friend = the friend you feel closest to
fall out = to stop being friendly after an argument
make up = to become friends again after an argument
daily routine = the things you usually do every day in order
get up = to leave your bed in the morning
look after = to take care of a person or animal
babysit = to look after a child while the parents are out
pocket money = a small amount of money parents give a child
argument = an angry disagreement
celebrate = to do something special because of a happy event
anniversary = a date you remember each year because something happened then
invite = to ask someone to come to an event
guest = a person you have invited to your home or event
close friend = a friend you trust with private things
acquaintance = someone you know a little, but not a close friend
extended family = grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins as well as parents
keep in touch = to continue writing or speaking to someone
bring up = to care for a child until they are grown
have a rest = to stop activity and relax for a while
hobby = an activity you do regularly for pleasure
spend time = to use a period of time doing something
get together = to meet as a group
lonely = unhappy because you are alone
parents = your mother and father
mother = a female parent
father = a male parent
stepmother = a woman married to your father but not your mother
stepfather = a man married to your mother but not your father
sibling = a brother or sister
elder brother = a brother who is older than you
younger sister = a sister who is younger than you
twin sister = a sister born at the same time as you
grandparents = the parents of your mother or father
grandmother = the mother of your mother or father
grandfather = the father of your mother or father
grandchild = the child of your son or daughter
aunt = the sister of your parent, or your uncle's wife
uncle = the brother of your parent, or your aunt's husband
husband = the man a woman is married to
wife = the woman a man is married to
single = not married
engaged = having promised to get married
wedding = the ceremony and party when two people marry
honeymoon = a holiday just after a wedding
only child = a person with no brothers or sisters
nuclear family = parents and their children living together
single parent = a mother or father bringing up a child without a partner
adopt = to become the legal parent of a child who is not born to you
wake up = to stop sleeping
have a shower = to wash your body under running water
have a bath = to wash in a tub of water
brush your teeth = to clean your teeth with a brush
have breakfast = to eat the first meal of the day
leave home = to go out of your house, for example to school
come home = to return to your house
do homework = to complete schoolwork at home
go to bed = to get into bed to sleep
fall asleep = to start sleeping
oversleep = to sleep longer than you planned
have a lie-in = to stay in bed later than usual
set the table = to put plates and cutlery on the table before a meal
clear the table = to take plates away after a meal
feed the pet = to give food to a cat, dog or other animal at home
walk the dog = to take a dog outside for exercise
chat = to talk in a friendly, informal way
text = to send a written message on a phone
call = to telephone someone
meet up = to come together in one place
have a party = to invite people to celebrate at your home
stay the night = to sleep at someone else's house
go for a walk = to walk for pleasure
go cycling = to ride a bicycle for fun or sport
go swimming = to swim for fun or exercise
play board games = to play games such as chess at a table
play computer games = to play games on a computer or console
watch TV = to look at programmes on television
stream a film = to watch a film over the internet
listen to music = to play songs for pleasure
play an instrument = to make music on a piano, guitar or similar
collect stickers = to keep stickers as a hobby
take photos = to use a camera or phone to make pictures
go shopping = to visit shops to look at or buy things
hang around = to spend time in a place without a clear plan
have a row = to have an angry argument
apologise = to say you are sorry
forgive = to stop being angry with someone who did something wrong
trust = to believe that someone is honest and will not hurt you
rely on = to need someone and believe they will help
share secrets = to tell private information to someone you trust
make friends = to start new friendly relationships
lose touch = to stop writing or speaking to someone
penfriend = someone you write letters or emails to but rarely meet
neighbour's kid = a child who lives next door
family gathering = a meeting of many relatives
birthday cake = a cake for someone's birthday
birthday present = something you give to celebrate a birthday
wrapping paper = decorated paper around a gift
invitation = a request for someone to come to an event
RSVP = a note on an invitation asking you to reply
have fun = to enjoy yourself
be in a good mood = to feel happy and friendly
be in a bad mood = to feel angry or unhappy
feel homesick = to miss your home and family when you are away
miss someone = to be sad because a person is not with you
look forward to = to feel happy about something that will happen
spare time = time when you are not working or at school
leisure = time used for rest and hobbies
routine = the usual order of things you do
chores = regular jobs at home
